1422843110451671046 [2021-08-04] @visakanv 💜 44 🔁 2
gonna be a bit oblique for this one

so- when you make it a practice to talk openly as much as possible about almost everything you think, see, come across, etc

eventually you will stumble upon certain "fault lines" or "hotspots"

it's sort of like taboos but not exactly...

===

1422844363734851585 [2021-08-04] @visakanv 💜 14
my frustrating tentative conclusion is one that doesn't surprise me, and yet it frustrates me anyway – there are some things that just don't play well in public, because the public commons is not ready for it, because we do not yet have a high-trust public commons
↓
1422844599207297026 [2021-08-04] @visakanv 💜 30 🔁 2
i've circled around this a few times, bumped into it in multiple contexts

the core of my frustration is: there are some kids who *only* have access to the public commons and nothing else, and if the commons is hostile and ugly, they will become that, too

https://t.co/iHc3CSnsDQ
  [Quoting @visakanv: the truth I hate the most is probably "people who are really knowledgeable are publicly silent about the juiciest stuff, because the upside to talking about it publicly is minimal, and the downside potentially catastrophic"  really sucks for smart kids in shitty social graphs]
↓
1422845184505647105 [2021-08-04] @visakanv 💜 15
so this is a constraint that wasn't so obvious to me (except intellectually) when I had a smaller following and could say w/ever w/o as much concern about cascading effects. I understand better now why ppl with big followings are often bland. it's humbling https://t.co/yhaUKY1rT0
  [Quoting @visakanv: @msutherl @nwilliams030 @KevinSimler @leashless @QiaochuYuan @matdryhurst @malloc8 @benvickers_ @nosilverv @bronzejaguar @vanishingmaze @Meaningness @nemesis_global @NoaidiX @SamoBurja @maxdashiell @dthorson @alt_visa @naval My $0.02: a lot of today’s established public intellectuals grew up in a different media environment than the one we’re living in now. They might have Opinions on it, but the more popular they are, the more they’d likely be lagging behind the frontier. Relevant WBW: https://t.co/qsFvHPFGfZ]
↓
1422845477913980935 [2021-08-04] @visakanv 💜 12
side-note, it's interesting to me how often I can find old tweets that suggest to me I already kinda knew something about what I'm currently talking about, and to then realize that, while I did know something about it, I also didn't, in important and hard-to-articulate ways
↓
1422846018106757121 [2021-08-04] @visakanv 💜 12
the part that's humbling is, I guess I used to think in some vague, hopeful way that, if I grow my following, I can choose to behave differently. and I'd like to think that I do still make a conscientious effort, I try my best. but there's also a "physics" to it that I can't defy
↓
1422846772309725184 [2021-08-04] @visakanv 💜 12
I am determined to find ways to subvert these limitations though, and I think there are creative solutions available if you're determined. The trick I think is to use intermediaries, use replies, to be subtle and artful, to reframe the problem(s)
↓
1422848124133863424 [2021-08-04] @visakanv 💜 15 🔁 1
I'm very thankful that we can have alts. I don't think it's psychologically sustainable for anybody to be a switchboard for a broader social ecosystem + remain emotionally sensitive

https://t.co/hYmXgEEgVz
  [Quoting @visakanv: having multiple twitter identities is transhuman]
↓
1422849050013880322 [2021-08-04] @visakanv 💜 7
reminiscing on this thread https://t.co/NMS7nWz07e
  [Quoting @visakanv: A long term tension in my life: I don't feel qualified to lead, but I don't see anybody really worth following, either. When, where and how did I inherit these annoyingly perfectionist standards and ideals?]
↓
1422851268792356868 [2021-08-04] @visakanv 💜 44 🔁 4
so here's a thing I don't think anybody specifically told me:

when you're on a growth journey, there are things that you can do at each stage of that journey, that you can't do at any other stage. rather than be wishful for the next stage, enjoy what you can only do now

rating.reasoning_summary: This strand documents the creation and multi-year maintenance of the 'Ingroup Map'—a Google Maps-based tool allowing Twitter community members to semi-anonymously share locations for meetups. The boundary object is the map itself (launched June 2021 by goblinodds and xsphi), which evolves from a simple directory (148 entries) to a 300+ pin infrastructure enabling real-world coordination. The arc is constructive rather than dialectical: the discourse is about technical maintenance (geocoding errors, privacy incidents requiring verification), periodic updates, and utility validation (people using it for travel, matchmaking, event planning). Evolution is medium (the tool remains static but its social function deepens), cohesion is high (core maintainers persist for 4+ years), and utility is high (enables concrete meetups, inspires similar tools like Partiful integration proposals).

essential_tweets.annotation: Pre-history: michelleakin's 2015 meetup organizing shows the latent demand for location-based community coordination
The Artifact: goblinodds launches the Ingroup Map with xsphi, establishing the core infrastructure (form + map)
Technical Crisis: The '0,0 ocean pin' bug forces goblinodds to learn coding, demonstrating the map's maintenance demands
Privacy Incident: Someone added without consent triggers verification protocol, showing community trust-building
Growth Milestone: 148 entries across 5 continents, validating the map's scale and international reach
Philosophical Context: visakanv on high-trust commons and public/private tension, framing why tools like the map matter
Application: goblinodds uses map for matchmaking (mimi10v3 seeking DC partner), showing utility beyond meetups
Real-World Coordination: puheenix uses map data to organize NYC karaoke birthday party, proving execution value
Feature Request: PrinceVogel proposes Twitter integrate similar functionality (Partiful clone), validating the map's design
Persistence: 2025 update shows the map still active after 4 years, with maintainers cleaning outdated pins
